svg.text: Circles first • Both-way handshakes • Privacy as structure, not settings

g.text: Two plans ahead. Your window is open.
Only people whose window overlaps can find you
One tap sends "who's in for Sunday?"
Intimate by default. Big only on purpose.
Nearby people whose free time overlaps
can wave. Both must say hi.
Inside circles there are no approvals — just RSVP.
A quiet signal. Not a post, not a profile.
Closes by itself when the window ends.
It is never posted anywhere — it only matches.
Same window, same vibes, 900 m apart.
If you both tap hi, we open a private room
to plan something real. Nobody sees
Pass quietly — they will never know
NO PROFILE BROWSING · NO COLD TEXTS
You both said hi. Say the plan out loud.
Court 3 is free at 5. Loser buys
Full profiles unlock once a plan is locked.
REPORT · BLOCK · PAUSE — ALWAYS ONE TAP AWAY
Court 3 · Aarav and Sara from today's overlap
PRIVATE NOTE · ONLY YOU SEE THIS
Recaps live only in the circles that were there.
Share per plan. Auto-expires when it ends.
No search exists. Strangers need mutual hi.
Boring by design. That is the point.
Silent, mutual, instant. They never learn.
Warm-room proposals are filtered to match.
Late plan? We check on you.
No reply, and we nudge the contact you chose.

svg.text: Every stranger is a mutual decision.

g.text: For your people — and the right strangers.
We text a 6-digit code. No passwords, ever.
Strangers meet through mutual windows only.
Circles, matches, data — gone on request.
Small stays warm. Cap it at 15.
Anyone with the link can ask to join;
not search. That is the whole idea.
Mutual hi, then a warm room
Splits, recaps, see you next week
Chat only exists inside plans now
Every message belongs to a plan
Settled by the time you get home

svg.text: OutThere v2: intimacy is the default, strangers are a symmetric exception, and safety is what the product refuses to make possible.
